_readme: US LANDING intelligence (Pro / intelligence tier). NOT public — kept out of map/data; surfaced via
the `pro-landing` CLI. Two datasets keyed by chain_id:
1) noncompete_cap — a realistic US store-count CEILING for a brand, driven by category non-compete /
radius clauses in US malls & plazas (the public map shows outlets that EXIST; this estimates how
many can EVER exist). US landlords grant category exclusivity (one coffee / one bubble-tea / one
dumpling brand per venue), so a late-entrant's addressable venue universe is capped. Fields:
grocery_anchored: blocked|limited|open}, cap_estimate{low,high}, cap_method, basis, confidence, as_of.
2) landing_readiness — an EXECUTION-quality grade for how well a brand is set up to scale in the US.
Seven 0-5 dimensions (see rubric) roll up to a 0-100 score + A-F grade (COMPUTED by the module, not
stored, so weights stay consistent). stage = preparing|trial|expansion|steady|contracting|exited.
risk_flags[] call out the article's failure patterns (no FDD, no territory protection, franchisee-
built supply chain, cannibalization, overexpansion). Fields: stage, dimensions{<dim>:{value,score,
Source insight: Zhixiang Chuhai (知象出海) 2026 interviews with the US-landing service layer (site
selection, construction/approval, marketing, capital). See memory cfc-pro-landing-ecosystem.

scale.na: does not franchise (score as direct strength)

luckin.cap_method: Starbucks holds category exclusivity in most A-malls/anchored plazas and gas-station traffic is taken, so coffee is pushed to street + secondary. Cap scales with urban-street density in top metros, not mall count.
luckin.basis: Article: 'if a Starbucks has already opened in a plaza, it will not allow Luckin to enter' + Luckin is starting from Manhattan street shops.

cotti.cap_method: Same coffee non-compete wall as Luckin; franchise model can push density but faces the same prime-venue exclusion.
cotti.basis: Coffee category exclusivity; Cotti opened street/secondary (Brooklyn first store).

chagee.cap_method: Plazas/malls grant one bubble-tea brand exclusivity, so the venue universe is split across many tea chains; cap set by Asian-heavy + campus + street venues where it can win the single tea slot.
chagee.basis: Article: a plaza 'will not allow you to open a second' tea/dumpling brand; aggressive $5-6 pricing helps win the slot.

mixue.cap_method: Low price supports high store count IF it can find small franchisees + cheap street/secondary sites; capped by the US scarcity of mom-and-pop operators and the one-tea-per-plaza rule.
mixue.basis: Article: Mixue wants mom-and-pop franchisees ('where can we find these in the US?'); low price is the growth lever (cf. Dunkin' 9,000 stores).

supply_chain.note: Coffee has strong local procurement; no kitchen build.

localization.note: Internet/app marketing strategy suited to US; 'has the right feeling.'

supply_chain.note: Core strength — makes money on the supply chain, not the store.

us_ops_team.note: China mindset; franchisee-recruitment gap in US.

localization.note: Price is the lever (cf. Dunkin' low-price playbook).

pace_discipline.note: Wants many small franchisees; US operator supply is the bottleneck.
